title.narrative: Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative: Bipartite social dialogue mechanisms strengthened between the employers and the workers organizations at sectoral and provincial level in Indonesia leading to signing of joint commitment for social dialogue and cooperation based responses for addressing labour relations challenges. The Indonesian employers' association (Apindo), API (Indonesian Textile Association) and APRISINDO (Indonesian Footwear Association)) and garment and footwear sector trade unions (SPSI, SPSI ATUC, Garteks) signed a joint commitment on 6th Aug 2020 to protect the health, business sustainability and welfare of workers in these sectors amid the Covid-19 pandemic. The joint commitment recognizes the need for a cooperation and social dialogue at the national, sectoral and factory level to devise solutions for addressing employment issues, implement safety, and health protocols during this period. Promotion of collective bargaining for addressing mutual concerns in the Palm oil sector, where 15 companies initiated collective bargaining to address issues related to improving OSH, applying equality and non-discrimination clauses Joint commitment signed in Apr 2021 between local Manpower Office, Employers organization members and local TU federations in Banten province to continue social dialogue process for improving workplace cooperation and collective bargaining for dealing with labour relations problems due to Covid-19 pandemic. The commitment reinforced social dialogue based responses at enterprise level factories in Jakarta, West and Central Java. The ILO provided capacity building and technical support to initiatives of employers and workers' organizations to engage in national recovery and to support their members – through TC programmes in specific sectors and regular ILO activities to support tripartite and bipartite social dialogue to strengthen workplace consultations and cooperation for strengthening bipartite industrial relations (focused on safe and productive workplaces, dispute resolution and promoting collective bargaining as industrial relations process).
